body:
I've ran into the exact same problem earlier. Running the ng build command with --verbose showed a lot of warnings and errors on the TerserPlugin part of the build. 

Eventually I stumbled upon this issue: [Issue 13939](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/issues/13939)
This comment in specific was what I needed to get it fixed: [Comment](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/issues/5618#issuecomment-450151214)

By default the memory limit in Node. js is 512 mb, to solve this issue you need to increase the memory limit use command —- max-old-space-size . 

I've added the following line to my package.json
`"ng-high-memory": "node --max_old_space_size=1024 ./node_modules/@angular/cli/bin/ng",`

From the comment on [Issue 13939](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/issues/13939) :

> When you use have that script, you can use `npm run ng-high-memory --` followed by the arguments instead of `ng` inside that project. Always use the double dash before arguments, otherwise they might not be parsed correctly.
That is not solution, that is hack :D. If someone can answer if this is a bug inside angular?
@petebacondarwin maybe you can have a look here?
Can you provide a reproduction of the problem? Ideally a runnable project or at least steps in how to produce one. It is difficult to debug without this

It sounds to me that one of the more aggressive terser optimisations is modifying the `$localize` calls in a way that the `@angular/localize` tooling cannot understand. Is it possible to build the app without localization and then find where there are instances of `$localize` in the built JS files?

@miki995 - I looked at that Stackblitz project but I couldn't see how it reproduces your error. There are no templates that use `i18n`, there is no code that calls `$localize` and moreover the dependencies on Angular are at version 6.1.9. How do I reproduce the actual error that you are reporting?
@petebacondarwin true, the stackblitz that angular github issue creator offered, goes to angular 6, I will create repo on github, just few minutes please :D

@petebacondarwin In our current project we do not yet use the `$localize` calls, and only import the `import '@angular/localize/init';` in the polyfills. So there are no dynamic translations yet, but we still get the error. It's difficult to make a reproduction, because it happens at random places where there is an i18n attribute

@PierreDuc - wherever there is an `i18n` tag in a template, the Angular compiler now creates a call to `$localize`. I assume that you are sure that the versions of `@angular/localize`, `@angular/compiler`, `@angular/compiler-cli` all line up?
OK so we need to work out what the optimizer is doing to the compiled `$localize` code that is stopping the translation tooling from reading it correctly.

Another small update. When you set the `optimization` to true, but you set the `buildOptimizer` to false, the bundling and localize works and you do get a minified bundle with the terser plugin (because that still spits out a great amount of warnings), with the proper localization. So it seems like the issue is in the build optimizer. Personally I don't know what the difference is between the two settings, apart from that the buildOptimizer uses the `@angular-devkit/build-optimizer` package. Reverting to version 0.900.0 of this package doesn't help.

This line in your output:

```
I18N_0 = "The actual string that's inside the i18n tag";
```

Is after the compile-time translation has occurred, which removes the `$localize` call and just leaves the translated (or not in this case) text.
